Directional mean and circular variance

Source: R/spw.R
dirmn.Rd

The mean direction of a set of directions, the mean resultant length R (from 0, directions spread evenly, to 1, all the same), the circular variance 1 - R and the circular standard deviation sqrt(-2 log R) (Mardia and Jupp 2000). Directions are given as angles, or as points seen from an origin (the directions of incidents from an offender's base, say). The mean direction of points depends on the origin chosen.

Usage

dirmn(
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  origin = c(0, 0),
  w = NULL,
  angle = NULL,
  lonlat = FALSE
)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

origin

For points: the origin c(x, y) (in degrees when lonlat = TRUE); no point may lie on it.

w

NULL, or one weight from 0 per direction, positive sum.

angle

Instead of points: angles in radians, anticlockwise from east (the x axis).

lonlat

FALSE (the default) when x and y are planar coordinates in one length unit; TRUE when they are longitude and latitude in degrees, which are then projected to metres by eqproj() about their own centre, and centres are returned in degrees. It is never guessed.

Value

A named numeric vector: theta (the mean direction in radians anticlockwise from east, in [0, 2 pi); NaN when R is 0), bearing (the same as a compass bearing, degrees clockwise from north), r, var, sd, w (the total weight) and n.

References

Mardia, K. V. and Jupp, P. E. (2000). Directional Statistics. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9780470316979

Examples

dirmn(c(1, 2, 0), c(1, 1, 3), origin = c(0, 0))
#>      theta    bearing          r        var         sd          w          n 
#>  0.9315290 36.6273216  0.8948002  0.1051998  0.4714971  3.0000000  3.0000000 
dirmn(angle = c(0.1, 0.2, 6.2))
#>        theta      bearing            r          var           sd            w 
#>  0.072363804 85.853859466  0.993136769  0.006863231  0.117361758  3.000000000 
#>            n 
#>  3.000000000
